opening.argument: The presentation centers on a technical system-design problem: protecting privacy and integrity when electronic records are used for model training. The speaker describes combining a Confidential Oracle with privacy-preserving systems to create “a full end-to-end security perimeter,” while also emphasizing that the user consents before relaying her health record to the entity training the model. The token-sale and accredited-investor material is framed within that same explanatory architecture: it begins, “For example, suppose that somebody is selling a token,” and illustrates how an LLM could assess investor status from a tax-filing transcript. These examples explain how confidential data and eligibility checks might operate in a system; they do not themselves present a direct solicitation or establish deceptive financial participation.

citations.quote: First is the problem of privacy. Alice is sending it into this environment but she has no idea whether her electronic record will be protected there. Second problem is one of integrity.
We end up with a full end-to-end security perimeter.
For example, suppose that somebody is selling a token, can only sell it to accredited investors
